narrative.overview: Precise, restrained, and information-dense: familiar desktop controls organize semantic knowledge, service operations, and inspectable observations. Components are precise and utilitarian. The work area carries the scientific content while compact navigation and inspection tools support it.
keyCharacteristics: Dockable desktop editors and a persistent service/navigation rail.
Theme-aware neutral surfaces, fine borders, and selective tonal emphasis.
Separate UI-state and semantic-type colors, plus declared service-role constants.
Compact cards, breadcrumbs, maps, metadata, and inspection history.

rules.name: The Role Separation Rule
rules.body: Keep UI feedback, service identity, and semantic type colors distinct in meaning. Semantic colors come from shared `Branding` constants and `KimStyle` token metadata, not a new local palette.

rules.name: The Theme Inheritance Rule
rules.body: Use the active theme's `-color-*` lookups for ordinary surfaces and text. `Theme.java` supports Primer Light/Dark, Nord Light/Dark, Cupertino Light/Dark, and Dracula; it falls back to Primer Light when the persisted theme is unavailable. Theme variants are not identical palettes. Existing fixed-color exceptions are implementation facts, not a mandate to add more hardcoded colors.

rules.name: The Density Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Preserve the distinction between observed density and a safe reusable default. Do not propagate the inspector's smallest labels into new primary controls without checking native text scaling and readability.

dos: Do inherit active-theme surface and text roles in JavaFX controls.
Do preserve distinct service-role and semantic-type color meanings.
Do reuse the existing card, inspection-history, and dockable-editor patterns where their behavior fits the task.
Do validate native focus, text scaling, and hit areas before treating compact inspection controls as reusable defaults.
donts: Don't flatten all supported themes into the light-theme frontmatter values.
Don't replace shared semantic colors with a new local color scheme.
Don't treat observed mouse-only wiring, tiny labels, or mismatched tooltips as endorsed design rules.
Don't treat HTML sidecar previews as production JavaFX components or proof of native accessibility.
